podcast.title: Left Big Wreck Temporarily
podcast.body: During a summer spent in Portland, Maine, Brian Doherty temporarily left Big Wreck, stating, "I can't do this anymore. I'm going back to New York." He returned to New York to work in construction and carpentry. "Brian had said, I'm out. I can't do this anymore. I'm going back to New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Met Ian Thornley at Berklee
podcast.body: Brian Doherty, a drummer, met Ian Thornley during his second semester at Berklee School of Music. They became fast friends and shared an apartment in Roxbury, where they began formulating ideas for a band. "Brian and I had met, it was in Brian Dirty. Yeah. We had met first, first year, second semester."

xref.title: Childhood Friend of Brian Doherty
xref.body: Dave Henning grew up with Brian Doherty in New York and roomed with him at Berklee School of Music, next door to Ian Thornley. He was an "obvious choice" for the bassist position in Big Wreck due to his existing connection with Brian. "Dave Hending was the obvious choice because he was, you know, grew up with Brian."

xref.title: Formation in Boston
xref.body: Big Wreck was formed in Boston, Massachusetts, out of collaborations between Ian Thornley, Brian Doherty, Dave Henning, and Forest Williams, who had met while attending Berklee School of Music. "It was formed in Boston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ian Thornley - In His Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Roxbury Living Experience
xref.body: While attending Berklee, Ian moved into the old Tremont Towers in Roxbury, Boston, with Brian Doherty and Dave Henning. This was an eye-opening and "scary" experience for a kid from Toronto, as they were living in a rough neighborhood. He quickly learned to "shut up, keep my head down and get where I was going, especially if it was dark." "it was scary is what it was. It was scary."
